provenance.method: AI independently reviewed the query-only cases as 50 SMART semantic templates and 44 literal TITLE_AUTHOR inputs; mechanically expanded only observed request/politeness/punctuation variants. No current parser behavior or original expected label informed these contracts.

field_policy: Only authored_fields are proposed normative field values. An omitted field is not an instruction to clear or relabel it. Null is an explicit authored absence. AI_REVIEWED denotes semantic review, not certainty for omitted fields.

field_representation.expected_author: nullable semantic author equality constraint; does not denote the literal author-side operand of TITLE_AUTHOR OR matching
field_representation.expected_title: nullable SMART title entity constraint; TITLE_AUTHOR literal projection is deliberately unresolved
field_representation.expected_exact_text: nullable exact-identity/literal payload; surface normalization is deliberately unresolved for ISBN and TITLE_AUTHOR
field_representation.expected_semantic_text: nullable soft topic remaining after explicit constraints; exact surface projection is left unresolved where underspecified
field_representation.expected_subjects: list of exact canonical scoped vocabulary labels
field_representation.expected_excluded_subjects: list of exact canonical scoped vocabulary labels
field_representation.expected_exclude_terms: literal text exclusions, separate from canonical subject exclusions

rules.SMART_WORDING_ONLY: In SMART, a request preface, politeness suffix, or terminal request punctuation does not alter the reviewed semantic constraints. This normalization is never applied in TITLE_AUTHOR.
rules.AUTHOR_VS_ABOUT: An explicit by/written by/authored by phrase establishes authorship. About/on/influence language concerns a topic and does not establish an author equality filter.
rules.ABOUT_IS_SOFT: An ordinary about/on topic remains semantic text even when a topic word also happens to occur in the scoped subject vocabulary.
rules.SCOPED_CANONICAL_NEGATIVE: A clearly named canonical scoped subject exclusion populates excluded subjects. It does not additionally prohibit occurrences of those words in title, author, description, or semantic text.
rules.UNLISTED_NEGATIVE_UNRESOLVED: When the excluded phrase is absent from the authorized scoped canonical vocabulary, this review does not invent a subject alias or a literal exclusion projection.
rules.MULTI_CONSTRAINT_COMPOSITION: Supported rating, year, format, availability, canonical subject, author, and soft-topic constraints compose without their order changing their meaning.
rules.COMMA_SCOPE_AMBIGUITY: In 'exclude Romance, Fiction', the final Fiction can continue the excluded list or name a separate included genre. Neither interpretation is uniquely established; choosing one as a unique gold label would invent meaning.
rules.TYPO_POLICY_UNRESOLVED: The intended spelling can be highly plausible while hard subject enforcement, soft fallback, correction notice, and execution policy remain underdetermined by the supplied contract. No forced decision or subject label is authored.
rules.SMART_ISBN_ACCEPTED: A syntactically valid ISBN identity request is accepted in SMART. An exact lookup may return no records; assignment or result existence is not required to establish that the request is executable.
rules.ISBN_LIKE_TEXT_IS_TEXT: A phrase explicitly asking for 'the text' does not become an ISBN lookup merely because it contains grouped digits. Literal-versus-soft text projection is left unresolved here.
rules.LITERAL_TITLE_AUTHOR: TITLE_AUTHOR matches the complete supplied literal query against title/author. It does not activate SMART by-author grammar or discard request-looking words, punctuation, or spacing.
rules.PROJECTION_RESTRAINT: Only explicitly authored fields are normative. Omitted fields remain untouched. Canonical casing alternatives, unspecified normalization, and unavailable enum values are not invented.
